commands.review_summary:

Reproducibility: yes. at source level, but not from a live run: current main returns before hydrating account data whenever the transport is not `xurl`, so bird-authenticated local mode cannot correct the seeded account.

target.title: fix: hydrate local account identity from bird transport
target.body:
## Problem

The web UI showed the seeded `@steipete` placeholder — handle, display name, **and avatar** — whenever the **bird** transport was active. `hydrateProfilesFromX` only ran under the `xurl` transport and bailed out early in local/bird mode, so the seeded default account was never corrected to the authenticated user.

## Changes

- Correct `acct_primary` + `profile_me` from `bird whoami` (handle, name, `external_user_id`) when xurl is unavailable but bird is authenticated.
- Parse the display name that bird prints as `@handle (Display Name)`.
- When the authenticated user id differs from the stored one, clear the stale seeded `avatar_url` so the UI falls back to initials rather than showing the previous user's photo. `bird whoami` cannot supply an avatar, so initials are the honest fallback.

## Usage

Hydration stays an explicit, idempotent command (no new startup side effects):

```bash
birdclaw import hydrate-profiles   # after init, or after switching bird accounts
```

## Notes / open questions

- I intentionally did **not** wire this into `birdclaw serve` startup to avoid running a `bird whoami` subprocess on every server boot. Happy to add an opt-in hook if you'd prefer the UI to self-correct.
- The avatar-clear is a deliberate behavior change on identity mismatch — flagging in case you'd rather keep the old avatar.

## Test Plan

Ran tests — `bird.test.ts` + `profile-hydration.test.ts`, 36 passing.
